To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of conduit-mounted prostheses in patients with aortic valve disease is associated with a high risk of early mortality and late re-intervention, and that there is a need for further research into the design of such devices.
the in vivo performance of conduit-mounted prostheses is generally superior to that of conventional prostheses and that the design of the latter is more suitable for implantation in aortic positions.
the use of a conduit mounted valve prosthesis has been shown to improve haemodynamics in the aortic position.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the interaction between the mechanical heart valve prosthesis and the human blood stream.
the design, manufacture and evaluation of novel prostheses for replacement of diseased heart valves.
the development of a new type of prosthetic heart valve.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the right patient, at the right time, by the right surgeon, conduit-mounted prostheses are the valve prostheses of choice.
the use of conduit-mounted prostheses has not been as successful as might have been expected.
, in terms of haematological and mechanical performance, the use of a conduit-mounted valve is not necessarily inferior to a conventional prosthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the conduit-mounted prosthetic valve is a useful and versatile alternative to other types of heart valve prosthesis, but that its design and performance can be further improved, especially in terms of haematological compatibility and durability.
, in the right hands, conduit-mounted prostheses are a valuable addition to the surgeon's armamentarium.

the conduit-mounted valve prostheses have the following advantages: 1) they can be implanted in the mitral position without the use of a prosthetic annulus; 2) they have a low thrombogenicity; 3) they are easy to implant and remove; 4) the valve can be implanted without damaging the subvalvular apparatus; 5) they are easy for the patient to manage and 6) they can be easily modified.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a new generation of conduit-mounted prostheses that will be more haemocompatible and have improved durability.
the conduit-mounted valve prostheses have a number of advantages and disadvantages when compared with conventional heart valve prostheses.
the conduit-mounted valve design has a great potential to be developed into an optimal heart valve replacement.
